title: LP Team
field: linear programming solver engineering, centred on the revised simplex method and above all the dual revised simplex method (pricing and CHUZR, bound-flipping ratio tests, dual steepest edge, sparse LU factorization and its updates, hyper-sparsity, parallel simplex) as built into research and production LP solvers; interior-point / barrier, first-order (PDLP-type) LP, crossover, presolve-centred and MIP traditions are not yet represented by a member
chase_hints: University of Edinburgh: ERGO technical reports on Julian Hall's pages (webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/hall/) and the Edinburgh Research Archive (era.ed.ac.uk)
solver documentation and open source (HiGHS: github.com/ERGO-Code/HiGHS, ergo-code.github.io/HiGHS; COPT: guide.coap.online/copt/en-doc/; COIN-OR Clp; FICO Xpress manuals)
Hans Mittelmann's benchmark pages (plato.asu.edu/bench.html) for solver context only, never as the member's own words

card_dimensions.D3: problem class and data model: the LP form handled (bounded variables, computational form, slack basis), the sparsity / structure / scale properties of the instances that the technique relies on or exploits (hyper-sparsity, density, block structure), and the assumptions stated for any correctness argument
card_dimensions.D4: algorithm and implementation design: data structures and linear-algebra kernels (sparse LU factorization, FTRAN / BTRAN, basis-update schemes), pivoting and pricing rules (CHUZR, CHUZC, dual steepest edge), numerical safeguards (tolerances, Harris and bound-flipping ratio tests, perturbation), task decomposition for parallelism, and any proof or invariant together with the device used
card_dimensions.D5: computational evaluation: test set, baselines (named solvers and versions), metrics (iterations, time, geometric-mean speed-up, performance profiles), hardware and thread counts, and whether failures or slowdowns are reported

members.name: Qi Huangfu
members.hint: University of Edinburgh PhD 2013, thesis 'High performance simplex solver' (advisor J. A. J. Hall); original author of HSOL, the dual revised simplex code that became the simplex core of HiGHS; PAMI / SIP parallel dual simplex (Huangfu & Hall, Mathematical Programming Computation 2018) and LU-update techniques (Huangfu & Hall, Computational Optimization and Applications 2015); later implemented PAMI in the FICO Xpress simplex solver and develops COPT (Cardinal Optimizer, Cardinal Operations). Not the medical researchers named Qi Huangfu at Zhejiang University
chase_hints: Julian Hall's Edinburgh pages webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/hall/ (old www.maths.ed.ac.uk/hall/ links redirect there): HuHa13/ (ERGO-14-011.pdf and the published HuHa13.pdf), HuHa12/ (ERGO-13-001), HaHu11/ (ERGO-11-007), PublicLP/, and talk slides co-presented with Huangfu: RAL10, IMA-NLAO_10, Lancs11, PPAM11, APMOD12, ERGO_301116, SIOPT17, EUROPT17 (each folder holds a PDF named after it)
Edinburgh Research Archive, era.ed.ac.uk/handle/1842/7952: the 2013 PhD thesis PDF
